RealmHound: Player Damage Sources

Implementation status of every effect that translates into damage the player deals, in the theoretical DPS calculator (Character Stats) and in Combat History. Generated from damage-sources-status.md.

Legend

Combat History numbers carry a provenance tag: SelfComputed (every hit resolved client-side), SelfPartial (some hits unresolved), SelfPending (no hit resolvable, count only), SelfEstimated, SelfReconciled / SelfServerReconciled (solo-kill reconciliation), Observed / PartiallyObserved (remote players, from server packets). Definitions: combat/types.rs. Every row stands on its own: notes name the effect and the affected items, and never refer to another row, so a row filtered on its own still reads completely.
ColumnMeaning
Damage sourcePlayer or Pet.
Effect nameThe effect identifier as used in the code or the asset XML (WeaponProc-style Rust names where one exists, otherwise the game's own tag/effect name).
Effect typeNative (from the item or ability definition), Enchantment, Consumable (the effect comes from using a consumable item rather than from equipped gear), or Seasonal (a modifier the game applies to the character from the season's rules, not from any item: Exaltation mastery, the Crucible's damage multiplier, the Blood Ritual tier).
ClassClasses that can reach the effect. all when the effect is on equipment every class can wear.
Equipment typeWeapon, Ability, Armor, Accessory (or - for account-wide bonuses), with the item category in parentheses where the game restricts it.
ItemsItem count, with full lists in the appendix. Items are written as Name (0x<object type>), the type id being what RealmHound resolves into the item's sprite.
Theoretical DPSYes = counted in the Character Stats calculator. Partial = visible but not folded into the DPS total. No = absent.
Combat HistoryYes = every hit is attributed to this source, whether self-computed locally or resolved from the server's own packet (ServerPlayerShoot for a volley, DamagePacket for a poison tick) against the target's live defense. Partial = part of the effect's damage is unattributable, or lands on a generic row. No = not attributed.
Has packetYes = the server sends the damage figure in a packet RealmHound reads: ServerPlayerShoot carries each bullet's pre-defense damage and names the firing item (ability volleys, side procs, summoned-creature shots), and DamagePacket carries the amount for damage the server applies itself (nova waves, poison ticks, hex detonations, bleeding, pet and summon hits). The target's defense is still applied locally, but the number is never simulated. No = no damage figure arrives: a weapon's PlayerShoot reports only the shot, so the damage is rolled here, and an effect that only changes stats or multipliers has no damage of its own. - = the effect deals no damage to observe.
NotesImplementation caveats.

YesYesYesDamage per use from the item's projectile range plus a stat-mod bonus; for orbs it is gated on consumed hex stacks. The server fires these volleys, so Combat History does not roll them: ServerPlayerShoot names the item and carries each bolt's pre-defense damage, which is resolved against the target's live defense and conditions (armor-piercing read from the item's own projectile data) and credited hit by hit to that ability's activation -- never to whichever ability was cast most recently (2026-10-16; re-checked 2026-10-17 against Wizard solos, where the volley accounts for every point of the fight). A bolt landing more than 2s after its activation, or a server-fired bullet with no observed activation (a weapon proc, an ability held across a map change), is filed under the equipped weapon instead; a bullet whose firing item has no projectile data is counted unresolved and makes the fight SelfPartial rather than being given a guessed value.

PetPetAbility Attack Close (404)NativeallPetall petsYesYesYesPower and frequency interpolated at levels 1, 30, 50, 70, 90, 100 from the Attack Close power table (7 to 200 damage per use). Pet hits and their damage are credited to the owner: the tracker learns the owner from the summoner_id carried on the pet's own shots (tracker.rs:2302-2306), which is also what registers those shots for local resolution, and falls back to proximity association only for pets that have not shot (tracker.rs:186-202); the pet's own hits are then resolved locally (tracker.rs:2510-2512), so a fight where the pet dealt everything still shows the owner's hits and damage, tagged Self-computed.

PetPet attack damage attributionNativeallPetall petsn/aYesYesPet hits are credited to their owner: a pet's own ServerPlayerShoot carries the per-bullet damage and the summoner_id that names its owner, so a pet-only fight still lists the owner with hits and damage; a pet that damages a boss with no shot in view sends a DamagePacket keyed to the pet's object id, which is mapped back to the owner the same way. Which creature counts as your pet is not inferred from proximity: it is the pet the character cache names (PetType), and a creature the engine cannot place is not credited, so a teammate's nearby pet (a Great Jelly, a Mermaid) cannot claim the hits. Ownership is decided at the shoot, not by the bullet: your own shots resolve through the correlated shot and pending_server_shots, while anything fired by the pet resolves only against pending_summon_shots keyed by (pet id, bullet id), with no fallback to the player's weapon, so the two per-shot values never mix (tracker.rs:2504-2515). Both are credited to the owner's row. One caveat: if a pet's shoot packet is missed, its hit is counted but left unvalued (tracker.rs:2568-2571), and at finalize every unvalued hit on the owner's row is estimated at accum.damage / resolved_hits (tracker.rs:3389-3393), tagging the row SelfEstimated. That average blends the owner's own resolved hits with the pet's resolved ones, and the counter does not separate them (unresolved_local_hits is a single figure), so a missed pet hit is valued closer to the player's per-hit damage than to the pet's whenever the player's hits are the larger share. Pet hits are also bucketed into the owner's current equipment for the per-equipment breakdown (tracker.rs:2573-2578).

Player: consumables and temporary boosts

Effects reached by using a consumable (SlotType 10 with <Consumable />): stat potions, temporary boosts, summoned creatures and combat windows. They are listed apart from the equipment tables because nothing here belongs to an equipped item, and none of them is modeled as its own damage term: the calculator reads the stats the character already has, while Combat History works from the server's stat values and the shots and hits it actually sees, so a boost the server reports does appear in its numbers. Each row states which of the two that amounts to. Appendix numbering here is not contiguous: A27 and A29 are equipment lists (see the tables above), because each consumable list is numbered next to the equipment list for the same effect. Consumable lists are A23, A24, A25, A26 and A28.

Biggest gaps, in order of expected value

Ordered by the expected gain in accuracy for a fight the player actually does. Each entry says what is missing today and what closing it involves. Everything here is still open. 1. Damage the client fires itself beyond the weapon's own projectile (the next one to close): BulletCreate procs (128 items, A17/A29), the enchantment proc groups that add shots or effects (AddOnPlayerShootActivate 67, AddOnPlayerHitActivate 71, AddOnPlayerAbilityActivate 37) and the shot-pattern rewrites (AddSubAttack / SetSubAttack, 40 + 40 enchantments, B4). A weapon's extra projectiles are rolled client-side exactly like its main shot, so Combat History never sees them and the calculator counts none of them: every fight with such an item is short by their damage, and B4 lists which weapons are affected. The mechanism already exists for the two Lethal Strike side procs (A29), which are resolved from shot geometry and counted once per trigger, so the work is generalising that path and letting each proc declare its own projectile and trigger. Worth checking first is the failure mode this shares: a shot whose projectile has no data for its weapon currently disables self-computed damage for the rest of the map (tracker.rs, "unknown projectile data"), and a sub-attack projectile is exactly that case. Replaying the four most recent captures (2026-10-14 and 2026-10-16) found no such shot, so the cliff is not being hit today -- it is one gear swap away, and an instrumented check for it belongs with this work. 2. Non-projectile ability damage with no declared window: Lightning, Trap, VampireBlast, Shuriken and DashTrail are counted by the calculator but not source-attributed by Combat History. Their damage numbers do arrive -- they are player-credited DamagePackets (see Has packet) -- but nothing in the packet names the effect, and their items declare no server-applied window, so the packets remain in the fight's generic packet_damage figure instead of an ability row (hence their Combat History: Partial). EffectBlast is condition-only and deals no damage of its own, so it is not part of this list. Effects whose item declares a window are credited to the activation, which is what the poison, threshold-poison and hex-detonation rows record: DamageNova waves (activationCount x time), a PoisonGrenade's duration, and a DetonateHex / on-detonate blast (600 ms grace). Which of the other effects fire a local volley as well is measurable rather than guessable -- combat_replay prints every ServerPlayerShoot and the damage each one resolves to, which is how ProjectileBurst and DamageNova were confirmed and credited to their source. 3. ST set bonuses (130 sets, equipmentsets.xml): pure stats, so the work is mechanical (parse, count distinct covered slots, add to the gear bonus before relative bonuses). Only the calculator is affected; Combat History already reads the server's stat values. 4. Conditions and buffs that change damage: a damage-relevant condition reaches Combat History only through the server's own stat and condition values (Weak x0.5 and Damaging x1.25 are folded into every resolved hit, Armor Broken zeroes defense, Cursed/Petrified scale the result), and the calculator models none of them. What is missing is the provenance: the 38 ConditionEffectSelf enchant mutators and the 71 AddOnPlayerHitActivate proc mutators are not parsed, so a Berserk or Damaging window opened by an enchant appears in the damage of a fight without being visible as a window in the breakdown. 5. Pet and summon systems: Rising Fury is missing from the calculator, and Combat History stores a credited creature's damage and hits but not the creature's own object type, so its row reads "Summon" with no identity. The Pocket Rat measurement above shows the type is known at credit time (0x4683), so this is a data-plumbing gap rather than a packet gap; the type is now stored (2026-10-16), which leaves naming the source item. That mapping is static game data and nearly clean: 247 items declare a summon effect (Activate 235 rows, plus 86 on ability use, 20 on hex detonate, 14 on shoot, 14 on switch, 11 on being hit and 3 on hitting), producing 271 distinct summoned entities (SpawnCreep 228, Pet 92, RaiseDead 63 rows), and 253 of those entities are spawned by exactly one item. The 18 that are not are almost all variants of the same item -- base + (SB) or shiny, the five Fishing Rod tiers sharing Summon Fishing Rod Blank (0x8712), the five Pocket Rat stack types sharing Summon Pocket Rat (0x4683) -- with only a few genuinely shared by different items (Summon Cat 0x89ae from Specialist Mace and Yarn Ball, the Necrotic Undead 0x16aa from Necrotic and Sacrilege Skulls). Ability and skull summons resolve from objectId / undeadId (skulls are 1:1, e.g. Bloodsucker Skull -> Bloodsucker Undead 0x16b0), while the proc-spawned ones (Flowering Kimono -> MV Kimono Summon 0x500a, Soul's Guidance -> Guided Forgotten Soul 0x6101) are exactly the proc forms the parser does not read yet, so naming those needs the same proc parse item 1 asks for. 6. On-hit proc triggers on equipment: the OnPlayerHitActivate and OnEnemyHitActivate tags are not matched by the parser, which hides 71 + 4 enchantments and the six ring/ability poison grenades (A19) from both sides.

Appendix A: items per effect

These lists are game-data inventories, not to-do lists. Every player-visible item that carries the effect is listed here whether or not RealmHound models that effect, so an item appearing below says nothing about coverage: a No or Partial row in the tables above applies to its whole list. The counts cited in the tables (101 items [A17]) are the sizes of these lists, and the per-list status badge under each heading repeats how that effect is implemented. To find actual gaps, filter the tables above for No or Partial rather than scanning these lists. Player-visible equippable items only, formatted as Item Name (0x<object type>). Internal spawner / proc objects (no <Description>, <BagType>, <feedPower> or <EnchantmentSlots>) are excluded, since their ids are never shown in game, and so are two other groups: unreleased content that cannot be obtained on production (currently T8 abilities, which is everything above the T7 maximum live abilities), and utility or legacy items whose effect cannot damage enemies (the stone, iron, emerald and diamond pickaxes, which only ever damaged event crates and are now vanity accessories). The type id is what RealmHound resolves into the item's sprite. An item that carries several effects appears once per list, and clicking any icon searches the page for it. Items listed as a bare type id have no display name anywhere in the game data; their sprite is still shown, and hovering says so.
